title: Sanitary Tees vs. Wye Fittings: Drainage Orientation Rules
description: Choosing the correct fitting orientation is critical for maintaining proper flow velocity and preventing solids from accumulating in drainage systems. A sanitary tee is specifically designed for transitioning flow from a horizontal branch into a vertical stack. Installing a sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain line is a major installation error; its short radius does not direct horizontal flow smoothly, causing waste to splash, lose momentum, and create clogs. For horizontal directional changes, plumbers must use a wye fitting combined with a 45-degree elbow to ensure a gradual, sweeping directional transition.
